newsitem.title: INDIA: Cochin Refineries says to restart soon.
newsitem.headline: Cochin Refineries says to restart soon.

text.p: Indian state-controlled crude oil refiner Cochin Refineries hopes to resume operations, which were halted earlier this week due to a water shortage, by Saturday morning, a company spokesman said.
"We hope to start operations tonight or at least by tomorrow morning," company spokesman Sanjeev Nair told Reuters on Friday by telephone from the southern city of Cochin.
Nair said the refiner had stocked 40,000 kilolitres of water, about 20,000 short of the required three days' supply before operations would resume.
"As soon as we get water of three days' stock, we will sart operation," Nair said. "We hope to get it by today evening."

Production at the 150,000 barrels-per-day refinery, located on the southwest coast of India, ground to a halt on Monday when water supply dwindled to 8,450 kilolitres per day compared to the refinery's daily demand of 22,750.
The refinery supplies petrol, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and diesel to the southern states of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
State Irrigation Department officials said low electricity voltage and leaks in supply pipes, responsible for the sharp drop in water supply, had been fixed.
Company officials said the state government was losing nearly 30 million rupees ($838,000) a day due to the shutdown.
They said it would take the refinery nearly one week after reopening to reach peak capacity. The refinery's annual production capacity is 7.5 million tonnes.
